Author: John
Reflection: Relevant to learning basic game-dev principles.
Well balanced. Since it's a group project, your group will be the main thing affecting your workload.
No exam. Assessment is fair, though may take a while if theres still just 1 TA.
Alex's lectures are entertaining, though as someone who had done a lot of game dev beforehand, there wasn't much new content (this will vary person-to-person).
If you've done game dev before/want to get into it. The things you cover are about game development in Godot/general game dev theory (juice, player experience, etc).

Learn GDscript early, and look into some higher-level concepts (namely Callables/signals in GDscript) that can let you do some nifty stuff (e.g. generic object/particle pooling). Also get a good team </3
